high.title: TSMC Contributes 63% of Science Park Revenue, Creating New High - Proportion Expected to Continue Rising
high.summary: The three major science parks generated record revenue of NT$5.8 trillion in 2025, growing 21.83%, with TSMC contributing 63% - the highest proportion ever. This represents a 5.3 percentage point increase from 57.79% in 2024, and significantly up from 42% in 2020. Integrated circuit business accounts for 83% of total park revenue, highlighting Taiwan's heavy dependence on semiconductor manufacturing. TSMC's dominance is expected to grow further as advanced process expansion continues at Central and Southern science parks. For investors, this demonstrates TSMC's overwhelming market position and Taiwan's economic reliance on semiconductor leadership, but also raises concentration risk concerns.

high.title: Foreign Investors Sell Nearly NT$600 Billion This Month, Capital Flows to Small-Mid Cap Stocks
high.summary: Taiwan stocks faced four major headwinds yesterday but closed down only 57 points at 33,342. Foreign investors sold NT$43.82 billion, bringing March total to NT$598.73 billion. TSMC dropped NT$20 to NT$1,845 ahead of today's ex-dividend date (NT$6 per share). While foreign capital flees large caps, funds are rotating into small-mid cap stocks, with TPEX index rising 1.3%. Market implications: massive foreign outflows reflect geopolitical risk concerns, but domestic liquidity remains strong with active rotation strategies favoring GTC-related concepts and year-end window dressing plays.

high.title: Semiconductor Price Increases Continue - UMC, VIS and Others Raise Foundry Prices, IC Design Houses Follow
high.summary: Global mature-process foundries including UMC, VIS, PSMC and China's Nexchip are raising prices up to 10% or more starting April, following memory and packaging price hikes. This represents a new wave of "chip inflation" spreading across the semiconductor supply chain. VIS reportedly issued customer notices citing rising equipment, raw materials, energy and precious metal costs. IC design houses, led by display driver manufacturers, are planning price increases to offset higher foundry costs. Market impact: mature-process chips are widely used in consumer electronics, automotive and industrial applications with higher penetration than advanced nodes, making this pricing power significant for foundry margins and downstream cost pressures.

high.title: Hon Hai: Strong Business Growth This Year - AI Server Shipments to Double, Smartphone Business Volume and Price Both Rising
high.summary: Hon Hai Chairman Young Liu stated during the online investor conference that AI server shipments (both GPU and ASIC) will grow multifold in 2026, while smartphone business will see both volume and price increases. The company expects strong overall performance growth and will increase capex by over 30% to record highs to meet robust customer demand. Liu revealed Hon Hai maintains over 40% market share in both GPU and ASIC platforms and is expanding CSP customer base. The company is progressing toward 2,000 cabinet weekly production capacity and strengthening its US manufacturing base as a key AI production hub. This signals Hon Hai's dominant position in AI infrastructure and strong growth trajectory in high-value segments.

medium.title: Five International Events to Know Before This Week's Market Open
medium.summary: US attacks on Iran's Kharg Island oil export hub have escalated Middle East supply risks, with oil prices surging and US stock futures declining. Brent crude is trading around $105/barrel after rising over 40% in two weeks. NVIDIA's GTC conference becomes the only bright spot amid three weeks of US market declines. TSMC ADR rose 0.5% Friday but remains at 16.2% premium to Taipei trading.

medium.title: US Stock Market Close - S&P 500 Surges 1%, Led by NVIDIA and AI Stocks as Oil Prices Retreat
medium.summary: US stocks rebounded Monday with S&P 500 posting best single-day performance since February, rising 1.01%. Technology stocks led gains with NVIDIA up 1.6% as GTC conference opened. Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 1.96%. Oil price retreat and reduced concerns over Strait of Hormuz closure helped ease market fears. NVIDIA expects at least $1 trillion potential market for advanced AI chips through 2027.

medium.title: National Team Deployed NT$80 Billion Last Week to Defend Market During Middle East Tensions
medium.summary: Eight major state-owned banks bought NT$49.2 billion net last week, with investment trusts adding NT$29.8 billion, totaling NT$79.1 billion in market support. TSMC received NT$23.4 billion in purchases from state banks and NT$5.9 billion from investment trusts. The intervention demonstrates government commitment to defending the monthly moving average as a key support level.

medium.title: Taiwan Stocks Supported by AI Supply Chain, Funds Expected to Return to Advanced Process and PCB Stocks
medium.summary: Taiwan stocks broke below monthly moving average support Friday amid Middle East tensions, but NVIDIA's GTC conference starting today may attract funds back to AI supply chain stocks. Experts expect the event to showcase Rubin platform with 1.6T network interfaces and CPO technology, potentially triggering capital rotation back into advanced process and PCB sectors for a technical rebound.

medium.title: Norwegian Sovereign Fund Selects Formosa Advanced Technologies, Analysts See Vote of Confidence in Glass Fiber Market
medium.summary: World's largest sovereign wealth fund acquired 1.05% stake in Formosa Advanced Technologies, the only new Taiwan glass fiber cloth company added to their portfolio. This comes amid strong demand for high-end materials in AI servers, high-speed switches and advanced substrates. Market analysts view this as endorsement of glass fiber market conditions by the global investment benchmark.
